service.name: Customer service
service.description: Handles customers calmly and solves their problem.
service.question: Describe a time you dealt with an upset customer. What did you do and what happened?
anchors: No relevant example or blames the customer.
Vague example, little detail on actions or result.
Clear example: listened, took specific action, problem resolved.
Strong example: specific actions, measurable result, and a lesson or process improvement.

data.name: Data skills
data.description: Uses spreadsheets or SQL to answer business questions.
data.question: Describe a report or analysis you built. What tools did you use and what did the business do with it?
anchors: Mentions tools but no real analysis or outcome.
Specific analysis with named tools and a clear use of the result.
Specific analysis, sound method, quantified impact on a decision.

teamwork.name: Teamwork and ownership
teamwork.description: Works with others and follows through.
teamwork.question: Tell us about a project you finished with a team. What was your part?
anchors: No example or takes no ownership.
Generic teamwork statements, own part unclear.
Own part is clear and the project was delivered.
Clear ownership, handled a setback, and the team outcome was concrete.

cases.answer: A guest at the front desk where I worked found his room double-booked at 11pm. I apologised, checked the system, and moved him to a suite at no extra charge after getting my supervisor's OK. I followed up the next morning with breakfast vouchers. He left a five-star review naming me, and I wrote up the double-booking cause so we added a duplicate-check step. Complaints about booking errors dropped over the next quarter.
A customer at the store was angry because an item she bought was faulty. I listened to her, apologised, checked the receipt and exchanged the item for a new one. She thanked me and left happy.

We launched on time and orders through the page were 20% of sales in the first month.
